title: The head and what it does
target: What the head in R.E.P.O. is made of before it reaches you: a controller driving hair, eyes and teeth, a float on curves, a staring eye with a beam, and a mouth that attaches.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A level with a living head in it
A crew that will say which way it went
A place to hide that is not directly under it

steps.do: Expect the head to be a machine with parts rather than one model.
steps.because: a controller brings together its visual, its animation system and the transform it looks at (EnemyHeadController, Visual, AnimationSystem, LookAtTransform)

steps.do: Watch its hair, because it moves on springs of its own.
steps.because: the hair has a parent, a target and its own position and rotation speeds, and a separate part tilts it with a random range and random times (EnemyHeadHair, HairParent, PositionSpeed, RotationSpeed, EnemyHeadHairTilt, RandomMin, RandomMax)

steps.do: Read its eyes, because they carry a target and a pupil that changes size.
steps.because: its eyes carry a target of their own, and the pupil keeps a size with a multiplier, a speed and a smallest and a largest size (EnemyHeadEye, EyeTarget, PupilSizeMultiplier, PupilSizeSpeed, PupilMinSize, PupilMaxSize)

steps.do: Learn the states you can catch it in, because the game names each one.
steps.because: the animation system has separate entries for beginning a chase, the chase and its second loop, returning to idle, spawning, despawning and being hurt (ChaseBegin, ChaseLoop, ChaseToIdle, Spawn, Despawn, Hurt)

steps.do: Listen for the teeth, because it chatters them while it waits.
steps.because: it chatters its teeth, with a shortest and a longest idle time for it (TeethChatter, IdleTeethTimeMin, IdleTeethTimeMax)

steps.do: Expect it to float and to look under things rather than to stand on the floor.
steps.because: its float is driven by a curve, a speed and an amount for its position and the same three for its rotation, and it can look under something with an offset (EnemyHeadFloat, CurvePos, SpeedPos, CurveRot, SpeedRot, LookUnderOffset)

steps.do: Do not assume distance keeps a mouth off you.
steps.because: the slow mouth attaches to a player with separate pieces for the top and the bottom of the face and uses a mouth in place of the player's own view (enemySlowMouthOnPlayerTop, enemySlowMouthOnPlayerBot, localCameraMouthPrefab)

steps.do: Watch an eye creature for a beam rather than only for a look.
steps.because: it carries a beam for each eye with particles of their own, and it has a sound for starting to stare and a loop while it stares (eyeBeamLeft, eyeBeamRight, eyeBeamParticles, sfxStaringStart, sfxStareLoop)

steps.do: Treat a mouth that heals as the one to keep away from the crew.
steps.because: the tick has a mouth with two lips and a state for them, and its healing is an aura with a health pool, its own particles and a loop (EnemyTickAnim, lipsClosed, lipsOpen, lipsState, EnemyTickHealAura, healthPool, auraLoop)

commonMistakes: Standing under a head that floats, because floating is what it does rather than falling.
Reading still hair as a head that is idle when the hair moves on its own.
Treating the slow mouth as a melee attacker when it attaches to the face.
Assuming an eye that is only looking at you cannot also fire a beam.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
